answer: Forward-secure signatures evolve the signing key forward in fixed time periods and erase each old key after use, so a leaked current key cannot forge signatures from earlier periods. The public key stays constant while the secret ratchets deterministically, and verifiers check the period tag alongside the signature. A farm that steals one key gains only the present spiral of time, because copper-era signatures stay sealed, and a sable past cannot be rewritten even with the newest key in hand.
